results.title: 12 PEOPLE KILLED IN KEBBI — POLICE INSPECTOR AMONG THE DEAD.
results.description:
12 PEOPLE KILLED IN KEBBI — POLICE INSPECTOR AMONG THE DEAD.

A series of attacks and reprisal violence has left at least 12 people dead in communities across Kebbi State, according to the state police command.

The affected areas include Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Koko-Besse LGA.

Police say five people were killed on October 26, while seven more, including a police inspector, died in attacks on October 28.

The command also says the violence followed an earlier incident at Samanaji Market on October 22, when local vigilantes allegedly attacked Fulani traders, leaving three people dead.

Homes and motorcycles were reportedly burnt, shops looted and residents displaced.

The police commissioner has ordered further security operations and investigations.

But beyond the death toll, a critical question remains: how did tensions escalate into repeated violence against communities, and what protection do residents now have?

results.description:
Gunmen Kill Police Inspector, 11 Others in Kebbi 

Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities.

The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse.

A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn
He said, "the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities," he said.

results.title: Residents of Waiwayi village in Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State were seen running for their lives as suspected Lakurawa militants
results.description:
Residents of Waiwayi village in Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State were seen running for their lives as suspected Lakurawa militants launched a deadly broad daylight attack on civilians. The militants raided Waiwayi, Karwa and Kestu villages around October 26 and 28, burning homes, looting shops and forcing residents to flee toward Koko town. Police confirmed 12 deaths across the attacks, including a police inspector, after joint security teams repelled the assailants.

Videos and local accounts, however, claim up to 20 people were killed in Waiwayi alone, with widespread destruction. The attacks highlight the continuing threat from the group, which is active in Kebbi and Sokoto and carries out raids and cattle rustling, leaving communities gripped by fear.

AllAfrica/Daily Trust reports that suspected Lakurawa and Mamudawa gunmen killed 11 residents and a police inspector in the Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State between 22 and 28 October, burning houses, looting property, and displacing residents from Karwa, Kestu, and Waiwayi. The casualty figures and group attribution are single-source and require police/state corroboration. Separately, RFI reports the WTO Aid for Trade review on 29–30 October 2026, noting Africa receives nearly 40% of roughly $800 billion mobilized over 20 years, but argues attracting investment alone is insufficient. The two messages are unrelated; only the Nigeria item has immediate security relevance.

results.description:
ZAMFARA — Oct 21–23

59+ bandits. Three-day siege on Birnin Tudu, Gummi LGA.

5 civilians killed returning from farms.
~1,000 cattle stolen.

Community vigilantes held the town. Without adequate military backup.
